slides.eyebrow: Moving to Boonton? The problem isn't you.
slides.sub: A historic downtown, a waterfall and the train, all off Main Street.

slides.title: Boonton Historic District
slides.body: Downtown Boonton's historic district runs along Main, Church, Birch, Cornelia and Cedar Streets. It's been on the National Register of Historic Places since 1980.
slides.source: NJ HPO Morris County register list; NPS NRIS #80002509 (Oct. 2026)

slides.title: Grace Lord Park
slides.body: Walk down from Main Street to the falls on the Rockaway River. The Boonton Heritage Trail starts here and follows the river through the Boonton Gorge.
slides.source: Town of Boonton; Morris Focus; NY-NJ Trail Conference (Oct. 2026)

slides.title: Boonton Station
slides.body: NJ Transit's Boonton station is at Main Street and Route 202 on the Montclair-Boonton Line, with parking at Main Street and Myrtle Avenue.

slides.title: Your Main Street walk
slides.tip: Touring homes here? Walk from the house to Main Street and the station before you decide.
slides.source: NJ HPO; Town of Boonton; NJ Transit (Oct. 2026)

caption:
Moving to Boonton? The problem isn't you. It's driving past Main Street. Park once and see 3 stops on one street.

Downtown Boonton's historic district runs along Main, Church, Birch, Cornelia and Cedar Streets and has been on the National Register of Historic Places since 1980. Walk down to Grace Lord Park at West Main Street and Essex Avenue for the falls on the Rockaway River and the start of the Boonton Heritage Trail. Then head to NJ Transit's Boonton station at Main Street and Route 202 on the Montclair-Boonton Line.

Touring homes in Boonton? Walk from the house to Main Street and the station before you decide.
